Docket 1.3.120

**Docket is free to try: run a full audit of any site without a key and see your score, how many problems each area has, and the most important problem in full with its fix. [Buy it once](https://kerr-affiliate-hub.kerrco.workers.dev/buy/docket?src=release-notes), $349, or 4 payments of $87.25, to see all the others, the ranked fix plan and the markup to paste. 30-day refund, no conditions.**

- *A sitemap plugin's browser view of your sitemap is no longer audited as a page.* Some sitemap plugins publish an
  HTML version of the XML sitemap and list it in the sitemap itself. Docket crawled it like any page and reported
  it for a missing mobile viewport, a missing description and thin content, none of which anyone needs to fix. A
  sitemap rendered for a browser, or served as XML, is now left out of the page checks, and the sitemap itself is
  still checked as a sitemap. A sitemap page written for visitors is still a page and keeps its checks.
- *Reviews signed with a hyphen are read as reviews.* A dental practice's reviews page showed dozens of patient
  reviews, each signed "- Name", and Docket said the site had no reviews or testimonials and told it to add some.
  Docket only recognised a signature after a long dash, and the first signature sat further below the "patient
  reviews" heading than it looked. A hyphen now signs a review after the end of a sentence, and a run of signed
  reviews below a reviews heading counts. Opening hours such as "Monday - Friday" are not read as signatures.
- *A short notice is no longer called a category listing.* A university department's 34-word COVID notice, with
  two links out, was described as an author, tag or category page, and so was not reported as the very thin page it
  is. Words from the site's menu and skip link were counted as if the page listed them. Only links that appear in a
  page's own text now count as its entries, so the notice is reported as very thin. Tag and author pages that list
  headlines are still read as listings.

99 checks across 13 areas.
